newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt mart girds for more new issues.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt mart girds for more new issues.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond market players expect Argentina, Italy, China and other foreign nations to join U.S. companies in bringing new issues to market at a healthy clip in 1997 following record years in 1996 and 1995, dealers said.
"There's nothing firmly scheduled in terms of issues right now...but there is talk of some deals currently in the works," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Argentina is rumored to bring a mega global debt offering of between $2.0 and $3.0 billion in late January via Merrill Lynch & Co, syndicate sources said.
Sources said they expect Argentina's debt offering to consist of longer-dated maturities.

Italy is expected to issue $1.0 billion in 10-year global debt in early January, syndicate sources said, while State Development Bank of China is expected to issue $300 million in 10-year yankee debt. Columbia, Finland and Israel are also rumored to be preparing near-term deals, they said.
On the domestic front, sources said they expect Aon Corp to issue $700 million in 144A trust preferred securities and TCI Communications Inc to issue $500 million trust preferreds securities.

Turning to the high-yield sector, Tenet Healthcare is getting set to bring a two-part debt offering consisting of $800 million in notes due 2007 and $500 million in notes due 2007, market sources said.
The deal is expected to be underwritten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities, which research firm Securities Data listed as the leading high-yield underwriter for 1996.
Multicanal SA, an Argentinian cable company, is expected to sell $250 million in junk bonds via a 144A private debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.

Zero coupon bond deals, which have grown scarce in recent months, are expected to reappear in early 1997, sources said. They pointed to talk that Optelcom is expected to issue $150 million in zeros, General Wireless is preparing a $220 million deal and UIH Australia/Pacific Inc which is expected to issue a $150 million zero coupon issue.

Other junk bond issuers expected to tap the market in the new year are Systems International, Corning Clinical Labs, Bresnan Communications, ACF Industries, Syratech Corp, Pocket Communications and Premier Parks, high-yield sources said.

Issuance of straight corporate debt reached a record $535.7 billion in 1996 beating the previous high of $443.4 billion set in 1995, research firm Securities Data Co said, while the number of issues grew to more than 5,436 in 1996 from 4,327 the previous year.
Merrill Lynch & Co, once again took top honors as the leading underwriter of straight debt, excluding mortgage and asset-backed securities, the company said.
Salomon Brothers followed in second place and Goldman Sachs & Co came in third for straight corporate underwriting.

According to Securities Data, combined public and private high-yield bond deals approached the record level of $73 billion set in 1993 with public domestic corporate bond issuance climbing to about $29 billion in '96 from $25.2 billion in 1995.
In the government market, the 30-year bond is off 33/32 at 97-3/32 to yield 6.73 percent.
